dossier.public_summary: The dip does not repeat the same depth: most transits show no eclipse and two nearby transits are much deeper, and depth is strongly different between sectors and between odd and even events. Centroid is inconclusive and the star shows large astrometric noise, so a variable blended eclipsing binary or spurious deep events best explains the signal, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth varies by factor ~5 and including a negative sector, inconsistent with a planet; sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source confirms change is real within SPOC 2-min (p_constant=7.394e-14).
Signal not repeatable: only 3 of 8 transits (two ~3x deeper in S70) carry the signal, others are consistent with no dip (depth ~49 ppm, -254 ppm, -4.2 sigma).
reasons.value: p_consistent=1.661848594709151e-57; share_of_top_3=0.948; outliers 2838 ppm (10.1 sigma) and 3530 ppm (9.8 sigma) vs mean 922 ppm

reasons.why: Odd/even difference ~50% points to two different eclipses at twice the period, consistent with diluted/offset eclipses in a blend or few bad events, not a consistent planetary transit.
Stellar astrometry shows significant excess noise, consistent with either variability/dilution affecting the photometry or a blended companion, supporting the variable-depth scenario over a planet.
